svg.text: Everyday English - Grammar
Were it not for: present
hypothetical inversion
MEANING
Were it not for introduces a hypothetical situation in which
a current condition is absent.
IN CONTEXT
Were it not for the grant, the research team would have to
close the project.
USAGE NOTE
This formal construction means If it were not for; omit if
and place were before it. It normally introduces an
imagined change to a current situation. To describe a past
counterfactual, use Had it not been for the grant, the team
would have closed. Choose the form according to the time
of the imagined situation, rather than simply when the
grant arrived.
CONVERSATION
A: Why does the report mention the grant so prominently?
B: Were it not for that support, the project would be
impossible.
A: Are you describing the current situation?
B: Exactly. For last year, I would use Had it not been for.
YOUR TURN
Rewrite for a past consequence: If it had not been for her
help, we would have missed the deadline. Model: Had it
not been for her help, we would have missed the deadline.
